exercises.paragraph: Use the ratio test to determine whether $$\sum\limits_{n = 1}^{\infty}a_{n}$$ converges, where $$a_{n}$$ is given in the following problems. State if the ratio test is inconclusive.
Use the root test to determine whether $$\sum\limits_{n = 1}^{\infty}a_{n}$$ converges, where $$a_{n}$$ is as follows.
For this exercise, let n start at 2.

In the following exercises, use either the ratio test or the root test as appropriate to determine whether the series $$\sum\limits_{k = 1}^{\infty}a_{k}$$ with given terms $$a_{k}$$ converges, or state if the test is inconclusive.

solution.paragraph: $$ak1/k\to ln(3)>1.ak1/k\to ln(3)>1.$$ Diverges by root test.

exercises.paragraph: Use the ratio test to determine whether $$\sum\limits_{n = 1}^{\infty}a_{n}$$ converges, or state if the ratio test is inconclusive.
Use the root and limit comparison tests to determine whether $$\sum\limits_{n = 1}^{\infty}a_{n}$$ converges.

solution.paragraph: Converges by root test and limit comparison test since $$xn\to 2.xn\to 2.$$

exercises.paragraph: In the following exercises, use an appropriate test to determine whether the series converges.

$$an=2(n+1)(n+2),an=2(n+1)(n+2),$$ which converges by comparison with $$p-seriesp-series$$ for $$p=2.p=2.$$

problem.paragraph: $$a_{k} = \left( \frac{k}{k + \ln k} \right)^{k}$$ (Hint: $$a_{k} = \left( {1 + \frac{\ln k}{k}} \right)^{-(k/\ln k)\ln k} \approx e^{-\ln k}.)$$

exercises.paragraph: The following series converge by the ratio test. Use summation by parts, $${\sum\limits_{k = 1}^{n}a_{k}}\left( {b_{k + 1} - b_{k}} \right) = \left\lbrack {a_{n + 1}b_{n + 1} - a_{1}b_{1}} \right\rbrack - {\sum\limits_{k = 1}^{n}b_{k + 1}}\left( {a_{k + 1} - a_{k}} \right),$$ to find the sum of the given series.

problem.paragraph: $${\sum\limits_{k = 1}^{\infty}\frac{k}{c^{k}}},$$ where $$c > 1$$ (Hint: Take $$a_{k} = k$$ and $$b_{k} = c^{1 - k}/(c - 1).)$$

solution.paragraph: If $$bk=c1-k/(c-1)bk=c1-k/(c-1)$$ and $$ak=k,ak=k,$$ then $$bk+1-bk=-c-kbk+1-bk=-c-k$$ and $$\sum n=1\infty kck=a1b1+1c-1\sum k=1\infty c-k=c(c-1)2.\sum n=1\infty kck=a1b1+1c-1\sum k=1\infty c-k=c(c-1)2.$$

exercises.paragraph: The kth term of each of the following series has a factor $$x^{k}.$$ Find the range of $$x$$ for which the ratio test implies that the series converges.

problem.paragraph: Does there exist a number $$p$$ such that $$\sum\limits_{n = 1}^{\infty}\frac{2^{n}}{n^{p}}$$ converges?
Let $$0 < r < 1.$$ For which real numbers $$p$$ does $${\sum\limits_{n = 1}^{\infty}n^{p}}r^{n}$$ converge?

solution.paragraph: All real numbers $$pp$$ by the ratio test.

problem.paragraph: Suppose that $$\left. \underset{n\rightarrow\infty}{\lim } \middle| \frac{a_{n + 1}}{a_{n}} \middle| = p. \right.$$ For which values of $$p$$ must $${\sum\limits_{n = 1}^{\infty}2^{n}}a_{n}$$ converge?

Suppose that $$\left. \underset{n\rightarrow\infty}{\lim } \middle| \frac{a_{n + 1}}{a_{n}} \middle| = p. \right.$$ For which values of $$r > 0$$ is $${\sum\limits_{n = 1}^{\infty}r^{n}}a_{n}$$ guaranteed to converge?

Suppose that $$\left| \frac{a_{n + 1}}{a_{n}} \middle| \leq {(n + 1)}^{p} \right.$$ for all $$n = 1,2 \text{,…}$$ where $$p$$ is a fixed real number. For which values of $$p$$ is $${\sum\limits_{n = 1}^{\infty}n} \text{!} a_{n}$$ guaranteed to converge?

For which values of $$r > 0,$$ if any, does $$\sum\limits_{n = 1}^{\infty}r^{\sqrt{n}}$$ converge? (Hint: $${\sum\limits_{n = 1}^{\infty}a_{n}} = {\sum\limits_{k = 1}^{\infty}{\sum\limits_{n = k^{2}}^{{(k + 1)}^{2} - 1}a_{n}}}.)$$

solution.paragraph: $$0<r<1.0<r<1.$$ Note that the ratio and root tests are inconclusive. Using the hint, there are $$2k2k$$ terms $$rnrn$$ for $$k2\le n<(k+1)2,k2\le n<(k+1)2,$$ and for $$r<1r<1$$ each term is at least $$rk.rk.$$ Thus, $$\sum n=1\infty rn=\sum k=1\infty \sum n=k2(k+1)2-1rn\sum n=1\infty rn=\sum k=1\infty \sum n=k2(k+1)2-1rn$$ $$\ge \sum k=1\infty 2krk,\ge \sum k=1\infty 2krk,$$ which converges by the ratio test for $$r<1.r<1.$$ For $$r\ge 1r\ge 1$$ the series diverges by the divergence test.

problem.paragraph: Suppose that $$\left| \frac{a_{n + 2}}{a_{n}} \middle| \leq r < 1 \right.$$ for all $$n.$$ Can you conclude that $$\sum\limits_{n = 1}^{\infty}a_{n}$$ converges?

Let $$a_{n} = 2^{-\lbrack n/2\rbrack}$$ where $$\lbrack x\rbrack$$ is the greatest integer less than or equal to $$x.$$ Determine whether $$\sum\limits_{n = 1}^{\infty}a_{n}$$ converges and justify your answer.

solution.paragraph: One has $$a1=1,a1=1,$$ $$a2=a3=1/2,\ldots a2n=a2n+1=1/2n.a2=a3=1/2,\ldots a2n=a2n+1=1/2n.$$ The ratio test does not apply because $$an+1/an=1an+1/an=1$$ if $$nn$$ is even. However, $$an+2/an=1/2,an+2/an=1/2,$$ so the series converges according to the previous exercise. Of course, the series is just a duplicated geometric series.

exercises.paragraph: The following advanced exercises use a generalized ratio test to determine convergence of some series that arise in particular applications when tests in this chapter, including the ratio and root test, are not powerful enough to determine their convergence. The test states that if $$\underset{n\rightarrow\infty}{\lim }\frac{a_{2n}}{a_{n}} < 1/2,$$ then $$\sum a_{n}$$ converges, while if $$\underset{n\rightarrow\infty}{\lim }\frac{a_{2n + 1}}{a_{n}} > 1/2,$$ then $$\sum a_{n}$$ diverges.

problem.paragraph: Let $$a_{n} = \frac{1}{4} \frac{3}{6} \frac{5}{8} \text{⋯} \frac{2n - 1}{2n + 2} = \frac{1 \cdot 3 \cdot 5\cdots(2n - 1)}{2^{n}(n + 1) \text{!} }.$$ Explain why the ratio test cannot determine convergence of $${\sum\limits_{n = 1}^{\infty}a_{n}}.$$ Use the fact that $$1 - 1/(4k)$$ is increasing $$k$$ to estimate $$\underset{n\rightarrow\infty}{\lim }\frac{a_{2n}}{a_{n}}.$$

Let $$a_{n} = \frac{1}{1 + x} \frac{2}{2 + x} \text{⋯} \frac{n}{n + x} \frac{1}{n} = \frac{(n - 1) \text{!} }{(1 + x)(2 + x) \text{⋯} (n + x)}.$$ Show that $$a_{2n}/a_{n} \leq e^{-x/2}/2.$$ For which $$x > 0$$ does the generalized ratio test imply convergence of $${\sum\limits_{n = 1}^{\infty}a_{n}} \text{?}$$ (Hint: Write $$2a_{2n}/a_{n}$$ as a product of $$n$$ factors each smaller than $$1/\left( {1 + x/\left( {2n} \right)} \right).)$$

solution.paragraph: $$a2n/an=12\cdot n+1n+1+xn+2n+2+x⋯2n2n+x.a2n/an=12\cdot n+1n+1+xn+2n+2+x⋯2n2n+x.$$ The inverse of the $$kthkth$$ factor is $$(n+k+x)/(n+k)>1+x/(2n)(n+k+x)/(n+k)>1+x/(2n)$$ so the product is less than $$(1+x/(2n))-n\approx e-x/2.(1+x/(2n))-n\approx e-x/2.$$ Thus for $$x>0,x>0,$$ $$a2nan\le 12e-x/2.a2nan\le 12e-x/2.$$ The series converges for $$x>0.x>0.$$

problem.paragraph: Let $$a_{n} = \frac{n^{\ln n}}{\left( {\ln n} \right)^{n}}.$$ Show that $$\frac{a_{2n}}{a_{n}}\rightarrow 0$$ as $$n\rightarrow\infty.$$
